transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net landline customer services, my name is Hannah. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Hannah, my name is Simon Taylor. I am a community psychiatric nurse working on-call from home, and I subscribe to your permanent Number Withheld feature on our landline so patients cannot see my private home telephone number, but a patient called me back on my home landline this morning, proving that my outgoing caller identity is being broadcast and unmasked!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good afternoon Simon. If I understand correctly, your permanent Number Withheld privacy feature has failed on your landline, causing your private residential telephone number to be broadcast to patients during outgoing clinical calls. Before we inspect your exchange line privacy profile, could you confirm your full postal address and your account security PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it is 19 The Oval, Leeds, LS17 6TG, security PIN 3810, landline number 0113 2491024.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Simon, that confirms your account details. Have you attempted dialing prefix 141 before dialing outgoing patient phone numbers?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I pay two pounds a month specifically for permanent automated number withholding so I don't have to manually remember 141 on every emergency call!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Could I place you on hold for two minutes while I query your line feature profile on the Yorkshire digital telephone exchange switch?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for holding, Simon. The exchange switchboard indicates that the permanent Outgoing Calling Line Identity Restriction feature flag was de-provisioned during an automated system database purge on Sunday.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Why would an automated database purge remove a vital security and privacy feature without informing me?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: System maintenance routines occasionally flag legacy supplementary service profiles for re-validation against the central billing database.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you re-provision permanent Calling Line Identity Restriction right now?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, I am submitting an immediate provisioning order to re-attach permanent CLIR to line 0113 2491024.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How long does it take for the exchange switch to re-activate the restriction?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Exchange service modifications propagate through the central line card registers in approximately sixty to one hundred and twenty minutes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So until the two hours have elapsed, my private number is still visible if I make a call?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, unless you manually dial prefix 141 before the recipient's telephone number.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Dialing 141 will guarantee the number stays hidden while the exchange updates?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, prefix 141 forces immediate localized call-by-call caller ID suppression on the local exchange loop.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I will write 141 on a sticky note on the handset for this afternoon's calls.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Obviously permanent CLIR flags require synchronized signaling tables on both local and regional gateway switches.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, I understand the switch synchronization requirement.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Simon speaking, I handle acute psychiatric crisis patients with severe paranoid delusions and aggressive behavioral histories! Having my private residential home phone number leaked to dangerous patients puts my wife and my young children at immediate risk of stalking and home invasion! I have had to install security locks on my front gate today because S-Net turned off my privacy feature! I am sick with terror and outrage!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I completely understand the acute terror, outrage, and severe safety concerns this has caused for your wife, your young children, and your home, Simon. Having your private home telephone number exposed to psychiatric crisis patients when you rely on confidentiality is a grave security emergency, and I will ensure this restriction is permanently locked and personally verify its status with exchange engineering.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Hannah, you understand why this is a matter of family safety.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am attaching an urgent priority safety escalation flag to the exchange service order.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What is the Openreach service order reference for this activation?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The exchange order reference is PRIV-CLIR-44910-Y.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: PRIV-CLIR-44910-Y, noted down.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have also set a permanent administrative lock on your account preventing any automated routine from modifying privacy flags in the future.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That will protect my family from future maintenance glitches.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Can we test dialing your mobile phone from the landline right now with 141 to verify manual suppression?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am picking up the landline handset right now... Dialing 141 followed by my mobile number...

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Watch your mobile phone display as the incoming call arrives.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: My mobile is ringing... Screen displays: 'No Caller ID'! Manual 141 suppression works perfectly!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That confirms that manual privacy masking is one hundred percent functional immediately.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I will use 141 for all clinical calls until the permanent exchange switch completes in two hours.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Once the two-hour propagation window completes, permanent withholding will apply automatically without dialing 141.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So we cannot test the permanent automatic withholding until two hours have passed?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Correct, the exchange switchboard requires the two-hour window before permanent automated suppression activates.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I understand. I will test dialing without 141 at four o'clock this afternoon.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have applied a ten-pound goodwill credit to your landline account for the disruption.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Hannah, that is very kind.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have documented your nursing duty status on the account notes for all future representatives.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That will ensure everyone treats the line with clinical confidentiality.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before we conclude, what was that Leeds landline number again?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: As I told you right at the start of our call, it is 0113 2491024.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Simon, the Leeds landline number is confirmed on the engineering order.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Hannah for your compassion and urgent assistance today.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It has been my pleasure assisting you, Simon. Please stay safe, and thank you for the vital psychiatric nursing work you do.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Have a wonderful afternoon, Hannah. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there any other landline issue I can assist you with today, Simon?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No Hannah, that covers everything.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net landline customer services, Simon. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye Hannah.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.
